sourceManifest.useBoundary: Concept and grade-level reference only; all student-facing clue, hint, definition, signal, and explanation text is original

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Organized collection of values used for analysis
clues.hint: Think of the numbers or observations gathered before making a graph.
clues.definition: A dataset is a collected group of related values or observations used for analysis.
clues.signal: The wording points to the collection itself before any calculations are made.
clues.explanation: DATASET fits because statistics begins with a structured group of observations that can be sorted, graphed, summarized, or compared.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Smaller group studied to learn about a larger group
clues.hint: Pollsters use only part of the whole population when asking questions.
clues.definition: A sample is a subset selected from a larger population for study.
clues.signal: The clue contrasts a smaller studied group with the larger group it represents.
clues.explanation: SAMPLE fits because researchers often measure part of a population and use that evidence to make careful conclusions about the whole.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Count or study that includes every member of a population
clues.hint: Governments use this kind of count to learn about all residents.
clues.definition: A census is a count or survey that attempts to include every member of a population.
clues.signal: The word every signals a full-population count rather than a subset.
clues.explanation: CENSUS fits because it describes collecting information from the entire population being studied instead of from only selected members.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Question-based method for collecting responses
clues.hint: It might ask classmates about opinions, habits, or preferences.
clues.definition: A survey is a data-collection method that asks people questions and records their responses.
clues.signal: The phrase question-based method points to gathering information through responses.
clues.explanation: SURVEY fits because it names an organized way to collect data from people by asking the same or related questions.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Value that sits far away from the rest of a data group
clues.hint: On a dot plot, look for the point separated from the cluster.
clues.definition: An outlier is a data value that is unusually distant from most other values in a set.
clues.signal: The phrase far away from the rest points to an unusually separated value.
clues.explanation: OUTLIER fits because one unusually high or low value can affect summaries such as the mean and may need special attention.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Difference between the greatest and least values
clues.hint: Subtract the smallest value from the largest value.
clues.definition: Range is a measure of spread found by subtracting the minimum value from the maximum value.
clues.signal: The clue names the calculation using greatest and least values.
clues.explanation: RANGE fits because it gives a quick measure of how far a data set stretches from its lowest value to its highest value.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Count of how many times a value or category appears
clues.hint: A tally mark table records this for each category.
clues.definition: Frequency is the number of times a particular value or category occurs in data.
clues.signal: The count of repeated appearances points to a basic tabulation term.
clues.explanation: FREQUENCY fits because a table or bar graph often starts by counting how often each response or value occurs.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Bar graph that groups numerical data into intervals
clues.hint: Its bars usually touch because each bar covers a number bin.
clues.definition: A histogram is a graph that displays numerical data by grouping values into intervals and showing counts with bars.
clues.signal: Intervals and touching bars signal this particular display for numerical data.
clues.explanation: HISTOGRAM fits because it shows how many data values fall within each numerical interval, making the distribution easier to see.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Dot graph comparing two numerical variables
clues.hint: Each point has an x-value and a y-value.
clues.definition: A scatterplot is a graph of paired numerical data shown as points on a coordinate plane.
clues.signal: The phrase two numerical variables points to paired data displayed with dots.
clues.explanation: SCATTERPLOT fits because it lets students inspect whether paired measurements move together, move oppositely, or show little pattern.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Pattern showing how two variables tend to change together
clues.hint: It can be positive, negative, or close to zero.
clues.definition: Correlation is a statistical relationship describing how two variables vary together.
clues.signal: The phrase change together signals a relationship between paired measurements.
clues.explanation: CORRELATION fits because it names the strength and direction of an association seen in paired data, without by itself proving cause.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Relationship in which one factor directly produces a change in another
clues.hint: This is stronger than just seeing two patterns move together.
clues.definition: Causation is a relationship in which one event or factor directly brings about another.
clues.signal: The wording directly produces a change signals cause-and-effect reasoning.
clues.explanation: CAUSATION fits because statistics classes distinguish direct influence from an association that may be explained by another variable.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: General pattern of increase, decrease, or steady change
clues.hint: Look at the overall direction rather than one single point.
clues.definition: A trend is a general direction or pattern in data, especially across ordered values or time.
clues.signal: Increase, decrease, and steady change point to an overall data pattern.
clues.explanation: TREND fits because students use this term when describing the broad direction shown by data, not every small fluctuation.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Overall shape of how data values are spread
clues.hint: It can be centered, skewed, clustered, or widely spread out.
clues.definition: A distribution describes how the values in a data set are arranged across possible values.
clues.signal: The clue asks for the overall shape and spread of values.
clues.explanation: DISTRIBUTION fits because it describes the full pattern of data, including center, spread, clusters, gaps, and unusual values.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Average squared distance from the mean
clues.hint: Large values mean the numbers are more spread out from the center.
clues.definition: Variance is a measure of spread based on the average of squared deviations from the mean.
clues.signal: The phrase squared distance from the mean signals this advanced spread measure.
clues.explanation: VARIANCE fits because it quantifies how far data values typically lie from the mean after each distance is squared.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Cut point that helps divide ordered data into four parts
clues.hint: Box plots use first and third versions of this marker.
clues.definition: A quartile is a value that divides ordered data into four groups with roughly equal counts.
clues.signal: The phrase four parts signals a position marker in ordered data.
clues.explanation: QUARTILE fits because these cut points help describe the middle and spread of ordered data, especially in box plots.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Rank showing the percent of values at or below a score
clues.hint: A score at 80 on this scale is above most scores in the group.
clues.definition: A percentile is a rank that indicates what percent of data values are at or below a given value.
clues.signal: The clue ties a score to a percent of values below it.
clues.explanation: PERCENTILE fits because it locates a value within an ordered data set by comparing it with the rest of the values.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Span between two values used to group data
clues.hint: A graph might collect ages 10 through 14 in one bin.
clues.definition: An interval is a continuous span between two values, often used to group numerical data.
clues.signal: The phrase between two values points to a bounded numerical span.
clues.explanation: INTERVAL fits because grouped displays often count how many observations fall within each chosen span of values.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Unpredictable variation caused by chance
clues.hint: A fair die roll shows this because the next result is uncertain.
clues.definition: Randomness is variation or selection governed by chance rather than a predictable pattern.
clues.signal: Chance and uncertain results signal this idea in probability and sampling.
clues.explanation: RANDOMNESS fits because probability models account for variation that cannot be predicted exactly in advance.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Reasoned approximation based on available information
clues.hint: It is close enough for a purpose, even if it is not exact.
clues.definition: An estimate is an approximate value based on reasoning, measurement, or incomplete data.
clues.signal: Approximation and available information point to a value that is not claimed as exact.
clues.explanation: ESTIMATE fits because students use data and context to choose a reasonable approximate value when exact measurement is unavailable.

clues.subject: mathematics
clues.clue: Numerical fact about an entire population
clues.hint: A statistic from a subset may be used to approximate it.
clues.definition: A parameter is a numerical measure that describes a whole population.
clues.signal: The words entire population distinguish this value from one computed from a subset.
clues.explanation: PARAMETER fits because it names the population value that researchers often try to infer from collected data.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Speed described together with direction
clues.hint: Thirty meters per second east gives both pieces needed for this quantity.
clues.definition: Velocity is the rate of motion in a specified direction.
clues.signal: Speed together with direction signals a vector quantity in motion.
clues.explanation: VELOCITY fits because it tells how fast something moves and where it is headed, unlike speed alone.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Rate at which motion changes in speed or direction
clues.hint: A car has this when it speeds up, slows down, or turns.
clues.definition: Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes over time.
clues.signal: Changes in speed or direction point to changing velocity.
clues.explanation: ACCELERATION fits because physics uses it for any change in velocity, including speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Push or pull that can change an object's motion
clues.hint: It is measured in newtons in the SI system.
clues.definition: A force is a push or pull that can change the motion or shape of an object.
clues.signal: The phrase push or pull points to the basic interaction that affects motion.
clues.explanation: FORCE fits because it names the interaction that can start, stop, speed up, slow down, or redirect an object.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Amount of matter in an object
clues.hint: It is measured in kilograms and is not the same as weight.
clues.definition: Mass is a measure of how much matter an object contains.
clues.signal: Amount of matter points to a property that does not depend on local gravity.
clues.explanation: MASS fits because it measures an object's matter, while weight depends on the gravitational pull acting on that matter.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Tendency of matter to resist a change in motion
clues.hint: A heavier cart is harder to start or stop because of this property.
clues.definition: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion.
clues.signal: The wording resist a change in motion points to Newton's first-law idea.
clues.explanation: INERTIA fits because objects at rest tend to stay at rest and moving objects tend to keep moving unless acted on.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Quantity found from mass times velocity
clues.hint: A fast truck has more of it than a slow bicycle.
clues.definition: Momentum is a quantity of motion equal to mass multiplied by velocity.
clues.signal: The formula using mass and velocity identifies this motion quantity.
clues.explanation: MOMENTUM fits because moving objects carry this quantity, and collisions often analyze how it is transferred or conserved.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Contact force that opposes sliding motion
clues.hint: Rough surfaces usually create more of this than smooth ones.
clues.definition: Friction is a contact force that resists relative motion between surfaces.
clues.signal: Opposes sliding motion points to resistance between touching surfaces.
clues.explanation: FRICTION fits because it acts between surfaces and can slow motion or produce heat as objects rub together.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Capacity to do work or cause change
clues.hint: It may be stored, moving, thermal, chemical, or electrical.
clues.definition: Energy is the capacity to do work or produce change in a system.
clues.signal: Capacity to do work is the standard classroom signal for this physics term.
clues.explanation: ENERGY fits because physics tracks how this quantity transfers and transforms while total amount is conserved in closed systems.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Energy transferred when a force moves an object through distance
clues.hint: Pushing a box across the floor transfers this if the box moves.
clues.definition: Work is energy transferred when a force acts on an object over a displacement.
clues.signal: Force plus movement through distance identifies this physics quantity.
clues.explanation: WORK fits because physics defines it more narrowly than everyday effort: a force must cause displacement.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Rate at which energy is transferred or work is done
clues.hint: A watt is one unit used to measure it.
clues.definition: Power is the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.
clues.signal: The clue asks for a rate involving energy transfer or work.
clues.explanation: POWER fits because two machines can do the same amount of work, but the one that does it faster has more of this quantity.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Traveling disturbance that carries energy
clues.hint: Sound and light are studied as examples of this phenomenon.
clues.definition: A wave is a traveling disturbance that transfers energy without transporting matter overall.
clues.signal: Traveling disturbance and carries energy signal this broad physics idea.
clues.explanation: WAVE fits because many physical systems transfer energy through repeating disturbances in fields or materials.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Maximum displacement from a wave's rest position
clues.hint: For sound, a larger value is related to greater loudness.
clues.definition: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a wave from its equilibrium position.
clues.signal: Maximum displacement from rest points to a measure of wave size.
clues.explanation: AMPLITUDE fits because it measures how far a wave moves from its resting line, which often relates to intensity.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Distance between matching points on consecutive waves
clues.hint: Measure from crest to crest or trough to trough.
clues.definition: Wavelength is the distance between corresponding points on adjacent cycles of a wave.
clues.signal: Matching points on consecutive waves signal this spatial wave measure.
clues.explanation: WAVELENGTH fits because it measures the repeat distance of a wave pattern, such as crest-to-crest spacing.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Bending of a wave as it enters a new medium
clues.hint: A straw can look shifted in a glass of water because of this effect.
clues.definition: Refraction is the bending of a wave caused by a change in speed as it passes into another medium.
clues.signal: Bending while entering a new medium points to a wave-speed change.
clues.explanation: REFRACTION fits because light, sound, and other waves can change direction when their speed changes in a different material.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Spreading of waves around an edge or through an opening
clues.hint: Sound can be heard around a doorway partly because of this behavior.
clues.definition: Diffraction is the bending and spreading of waves around obstacles or through openings.
clues.signal: Around an edge or through an opening signals this wave behavior.
clues.explanation: DIFFRACTION fits because waves do not always travel only in straight lines; they can spread after passing barriers or gaps.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Flow rate of electric charge
clues.hint: Amperes are the units used for this quantity.
clues.definition: Current is the rate at which electric charge flows past a point in a circuit.
clues.signal: Flow rate of electric charge identifies a basic circuit quantity.
clues.explanation: CURRENT fits because it measures how much electric charge passes through part of a circuit each second.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Electric potential difference measured in volts
clues.hint: A battery label often gives this value.
clues.definition: Voltage is electric potential difference, or energy transferred per unit charge.
clues.signal: Measured in volts points to electric potential difference.
clues.explanation: VOLTAGE fits because it describes the push per charge that can drive electric current through a circuit.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Opposition to electric charge flow in a circuit
clues.hint: Ohms are the units used to measure it.
clues.definition: Resistance is opposition to the flow of electric current in a material or circuit component.
clues.signal: Opposition to charge flow signals a circuit property measured in ohms.
clues.explanation: RESISTANCE fits because materials and components can limit current, converting some electrical energy into heat or other forms.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Complete path that lets electric charge flow
clues.hint: A bulb lights only when this path is closed.
clues.definition: A circuit is a connected path through which electric charge can flow.
clues.signal: Complete path and electric charge flow identify a basic electricity structure.
clues.explanation: CIRCUIT fits because current requires a continuous path through connected components and a source of electrical energy.

clues.subject: science
clues.clue: Force-related phenomenon involving poles and fields
clues.hint: Compass needles respond to this interaction from Earth.
clues.definition: Magnetism is the physical phenomenon involving magnetic fields and forces between poles, currents, or materials.
clues.signal: Poles and fields signal the attraction and repulsion studied in this topic.
clues.explanation: MAGNETISM fits because it explains effects such as compass alignment, magnetic attraction, and forces near electric currents.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Angular position north or south of the equator
clues.hint: Lines for this measurement run east-west across a map.
clues.definition: Latitude is angular distance north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.
clues.signal: North or south of the equator points to one coordinate used to locate places.
clues.explanation: LATITUDE fits because it identifies how far a place lies above or below the equator on Earth's grid.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Angular position east or west of the prime meridian
clues.hint: Lines for this coordinate meet at the poles.
clues.definition: Longitude is angular distance east or west of the prime meridian, measured in degrees.
clues.signal: East or west of the prime meridian identifies the other major map coordinate.
clues.explanation: LONGITUDE fits because it locates a place's east-west position on Earth's coordinate grid.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Imaginary circle halfway between Earth's poles
clues.hint: It marks 0 degrees latitude.
clues.definition: The equator is the imaginary line around Earth halfway between the North and South Poles.
clues.signal: Halfway between Earth's poles points to the global reference line at zero degrees.
clues.explanation: EQUATOR fits because this line divides Earth into northern and southern halves and anchors latitude measurements.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Line of longitude running from pole to pole
clues.hint: The prime one passes through Greenwich, England.
clues.definition: A meridian is an imaginary line of longitude connecting the North and South Poles.
clues.signal: Pole to pole and longitude indicate a north-south map reference line.
clues.explanation: MERIDIAN fits because each such line helps measure how far east or west a place is from the prime reference line.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Half of Earth divided by a major imaginary line
clues.hint: Northern and Southern are two examples.
clues.definition: A hemisphere is one half of Earth, commonly divided by the equator or a prime meridian reference.
clues.signal: Half of Earth signals a broad spatial division used on maps.
clues.explanation: HEMISPHERE fits because geographers use this term to describe large halves of the globe for location and comparison.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Shape and surface features of a place
clues.hint: Contour lines on a map help show it.
clues.definition: Topography is the arrangement of natural and human-made surface features in an area.
clues.signal: Surface features and shape point to the physical form of land.
clues.explanation: TOPOGRAPHY fits because it describes the hills, valleys, plains, and other features that shape a place's surface.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Height of a place above sea level
clues.hint: Mountain towns usually have a larger value than coastal towns.
clues.definition: Elevation is the height of a location above or below a reference level, usually sea level.
clues.signal: Height above sea level identifies a common physical geography measurement.
clues.explanation: ELEVATION fits because maps and geographic descriptions use it to compare how high locations are.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: High, mostly flat landform
clues.hint: It is raised like a tableland rather than peaked like a mountain.
clues.definition: A plateau is an elevated area of relatively flat land.
clues.signal: High and mostly flat identify a raised landform.
clues.explanation: PLATEAU fits because it names a broad, elevated land area that is flatter than a mountain range.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Narrow strip of land connecting two larger land areas
clues.hint: Panama is a famous example of this landform.
clues.definition: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land that connects two larger land areas and has water on two sides.
clues.signal: Narrow strip connecting larger land areas signals a land bridge.
clues.explanation: ISTHMUS fits because it names the geography feature that links landmasses while separating bodies of water.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Landform almost surrounded by water
clues.hint: Florida is a familiar U.S. example.
clues.definition: A peninsula is a piece of land surrounded by water on most sides while still connected to a larger land area.
clues.signal: Almost surrounded by water points to a landform that remains attached.
clues.explanation: PENINSULA fits because it describes land extending into water while keeping a connection to a larger landmass.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Group or chain of islands
clues.hint: Japan and the Philippines are examples at country scale.
clues.definition: An archipelago is a group, chain, or cluster of islands.
clues.signal: Group or chain of islands directly identifies this land-and-water term.
clues.explanation: ARCHIPELAGO fits because it names a set of islands considered together as a geographic unit.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Landform at a river mouth built from deposited sediment
clues.hint: It often forms where a river slows as it enters a sea or lake.
clues.definition: A delta is a landform made of sediment deposited where a river enters standing water.
clues.signal: River mouth and deposited sediment signal this landform.
clues.explanation: DELTA fits because rivers can drop sediment at their mouths, gradually building new land in a fanlike area.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Smaller stream that flows into a larger river
clues.hint: It adds water to the main channel.
clues.definition: A tributary is a stream or river that flows into a larger stream or river.
clues.signal: Flows into a larger river points to a feeder waterway.
clues.explanation: TRIBUTARY fits because river systems include smaller waterways that join and add flow to larger channels.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Area drained by a river and its connected streams
clues.hint: Rain falling within it eventually flows toward the same river system.
clues.definition: A basin is an area of land drained by a river system or a low area that collects water or sediment.
clues.signal: Drained by a river and connected streams points to a watershed-like region.
clues.explanation: BASIN fits because geographers use it to describe the land area linked by drainage into a shared river system.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Science and skill of making maps
clues.hint: People in this field decide projections, symbols, labels, and scale.
clues.definition: Cartography is the study and practice of designing and making maps.
clues.signal: Making maps points to the specialized field behind map design.
clues.explanation: CARTOGRAPHY fits because it combines geographic knowledge, measurement, and design choices to represent places on maps.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Map ratio comparing drawn distance with real distance
clues.hint: One inch on a map might stand for ten miles on the ground.
clues.definition: Scale is the relationship between distance on a map and actual distance on Earth.
clues.signal: Comparing drawn distance with real distance signals a map measurement tool.
clues.explanation: SCALE fits because it lets readers convert map measurements into real-world distances.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Area defined by shared physical or human features
clues.hint: The Corn Belt is one example in the United States.
clues.definition: A region is an area grouped together because it has shared characteristics.
clues.signal: Shared features point to an area grouped for geographic study.
clues.explanation: REGION fits because geographers organize places by common traits such as climate, economy, language, or landforms.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: People living in a particular place
clues.hint: A city can grow when more residents move in or are born there.
clues.definition: Population is the number or group of people living in a defined area.
clues.signal: People living in a place points to a core human geography measure.
clues.explanation: POPULATION fits because geographers compare how many people live in different places and how those numbers change.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Place where people establish a community
clues.hint: It may be rural, suburban, or urban.
clues.definition: A settlement is a place where people live and establish homes, services, and community life.
clues.signal: People establish a community points to a human geography term for inhabited places.
clues.explanation: SETTLEMENT fits because geography studies where communities form and how their locations relate to resources, transport, and land use.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Process by which cities grow and attract more people
clues.hint: It changes land use, housing, transportation, and services.
clues.definition: Urbanization is the growth of cities and the increasing share of people living in urban areas.
clues.signal: Cities grow and attract more people identifies a major human geography process.
clues.explanation: URBANIZATION fits because it describes the shift toward city living and the spatial changes that follow.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Form or method used to cast a vote
clues.hint: It may be paper, electronic, or mailed in.
clues.definition: A ballot is the form, device, or method by which a voter records choices in an election.
clues.signal: Cast a vote points to the object or method used to record a choice.
clues.explanation: BALLOT fits because voters use it to select candidates, approve measures, or express official choices.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Public process for choosing leaders or deciding measures
clues.hint: Voters participate in this process on scheduled dates.
clues.definition: An election is a formal process in which voters choose leaders or decide public questions.
clues.signal: Choosing leaders or deciding measures signals a formal voting process.
clues.explanation: ELECTION fits because democratic systems use organized voting to fill offices and decide certain policy questions.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Person chosen by voters to act for them in government
clues.hint: This official speaks and votes on behalf of constituents.
clues.definition: A representative is an elected person who acts and votes for constituents in government.
clues.signal: Chosen by voters to act for them points to an elected voice in government.
clues.explanation: REPRESENTATIVE fits because representative government relies on officials who make decisions on behalf of the people who elected them.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Upper chamber of the U.S. Congress
clues.hint: Each state has two members in this chamber.
clues.definition: The Senate is the upper chamber of the United States Congress, with two members from each state.
clues.signal: Upper chamber and two members per state identify this part of Congress.
clues.explanation: SENATE fits because it names the congressional chamber that gives equal representation to states regardless of population.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: National lawmaking body with two chambers in the United States
clues.hint: Its chambers are the House and a body with two members per state.
clues.definition: Congress is the national legislative body of the United States, made up of the House of Representatives and the Senate.
clues.signal: Two chambers and national lawmaking identify the federal legislative body.
clues.explanation: CONGRESS fits because it is the branch body that writes federal laws, controls funding, and represents states and districts.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Group of executive advisers who lead major departments
clues.hint: In the U.S., members include department secretaries and the attorney general.
clues.definition: The Cabinet is a group of top executive branch advisers, often including leaders of major departments.
clues.signal: Executive advisers and department leaders point to this governing group.
clues.explanation: CABINET fits because presidents and governors rely on these department heads for advice and administration.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Executive rejection of a bill passed by lawmakers
clues.hint: Lawmakers may try to override it with enough votes.
clues.definition: A veto is an executive action rejecting a bill and preventing it from becoming law unless overridden.
clues.signal: Executive rejection of a bill identifies a check on the legislative branch.
clues.explanation: VETO fits because it lets an executive block legislation, while an override process can preserve legislative power.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Government body responsible for making laws
clues.hint: A state can have one with two chambers or one chamber.
clues.definition: A legislature is a government body with authority to make, amend, or repeal laws.
clues.signal: Responsible for making laws points to the legislative function.
clues.explanation: LEGISLATURE fits because it names the body that debates and passes laws at national, state, or local levels.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Legal authority over a place, person, or type of case
clues.hint: A court must have this before it can decide a dispute.
clues.definition: Jurisdiction is the legal authority of a court or government body over certain people, places, or issues.
clues.signal: Legal authority over a case or place signals this civics and law term.
clues.explanation: JURISDICTION fits because courts and agencies can act only within the boundaries of authority given to them.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Supreme authority of a state to govern itself
clues.hint: Independent countries claim this power within their borders.
clues.definition: Sovereignty is the supreme authority of a state or people to govern independently.
clues.signal: Supreme authority and govern itself point to political independence.
clues.explanation: SOVEREIGNTY fits because it names the power of a government or people to make final decisions within a territory.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Legal protection requiring fair steps before loss of life, liberty, or property
clues.hint: Notice and a fair hearing are common parts of this protection.
clues.definition: Due process is the constitutional requirement that government follow fair legal procedures before depriving people of protected rights.
clues.signal: Fair legal steps before loss of liberty or property signals a constitutional safeguard.
clues.explanation: DUEPROCESS fits because it protects people from arbitrary government action by requiring lawful and fair procedures.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Request for a higher court to review a decision
clues.hint: It usually argues that a legal mistake affected the outcome.
clues.definition: An appeal is a request asking a higher court to review and possibly change a lower court decision.
clues.signal: Higher court review identifies this legal procedure.
clues.explanation: APPEAL fits because it gives a party a way to challenge a court decision through a reviewing court.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Earlier court decision used as a guide for later cases
clues.hint: Judges may rely on it when similar facts or legal issues appear.
clues.definition: Precedent is an earlier legal decision that guides courts deciding similar later cases.
clues.signal: Earlier decision used as a guide points to a legal reasoning tool.
clues.explanation: PRECEDENT fits because courts often look to past rulings for consistency when similar legal questions arise.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Formal request sent to government by people seeking action
clues.hint: It may include many signatures from supporters.
clues.definition: A petition is a formal written request asking an authority or government to take action.
clues.signal: Formal request and signatures point to a civic participation tool.
clues.explanation: PETITION fits because people use it to ask officials or institutions to address a problem or change a policy.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Local law passed by a city or town government
clues.hint: Noise rules and zoning rules are often examples.
clues.definition: An ordinance is a law or regulation enacted by a local government.
clues.signal: Local law points to a rule made by municipal authority.
clues.explanation: ORDINANCE fits because cities and towns use these laws to manage local issues such as land use, safety, and public behavior.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: City or town with its own local government
clues.hint: It may provide services such as roads, parks, and water systems.
clues.definition: A municipality is a city, town, or other local government unit with authority over local affairs.
clues.signal: City or town with local government identifies this civic unit.
clues.explanation: MUNICIPALITY fits because it names a local government that manages community services and rules within its boundaries.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Direct vote by citizens on a proposed law or policy
clues.hint: Instead of only choosing officials, voters decide the issue itself.
clues.definition: A referendum is a direct vote in which voters approve or reject a law, proposal, or policy question.
clues.signal: Direct vote on a proposed law points to this form of citizen decision-making.
clues.explanation: REFERENDUM fits because it lets voters decide a specific public question rather than only electing representatives.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Right to vote in political elections
clues.hint: Historical movements fought to expand this right to excluded groups.
clues.definition: Suffrage is the right to vote in political elections.
clues.signal: Right to vote identifies a core term in democratic participation history.
clues.explanation: SUFFRAGE fits because it names access to voting, a central issue in many civil rights movements.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Effort to influence public officials on policy
clues.hint: Interest groups often do this by meeting with lawmakers.
clues.definition: Lobbying is the act of trying to influence government officials or public policy decisions.
clues.signal: Influence public officials points to organized advocacy directed at government.
clues.explanation: LOBBYING fits because individuals and groups use communication and advocacy to persuade officials about laws or regulations.

clues.subject: social-studies
clues.clue: Current officeholder running or serving in a public position
clues.hint: This candidate may already be known to voters from holding the job.
clues.definition: An incumbent is a person who currently holds a political office or official position.
clues.signal: Current officeholder identifies the election and government term.
clues.explanation: INCUMBENT fits because elections often compare challengers with the person who already holds the office.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Recurring element that helps develop a larger idea
clues.hint: A repeated image, sound, or object can serve this purpose.
clues.definition: A motif is a recurring element in a text that contributes to a larger idea or pattern.
clues.signal: Recurring element points to a repeated feature with interpretive importance.
clues.explanation: MOTIF fits because readers track repeated details to understand how a text builds meaning over time.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Use of an object, action, or image to suggest deeper meaning
clues.hint: A storm in a story might stand for emotional conflict.
clues.definition: Symbolism is the use of something concrete to represent a larger idea, quality, or theme.
clues.signal: Suggest deeper meaning points to a concrete detail standing for an abstract idea.
clues.explanation: SYMBOLISM fits because readers interpret objects, colors, actions, or images that represent more than their literal role.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Descriptive language that appeals to the senses
clues.hint: Look for details involving sight, sound, smell, taste, or touch.
clues.definition: Imagery is descriptive language that creates sensory experience for a reader.
clues.signal: Appeals to the senses identifies language that helps readers imagine experience.
clues.explanation: IMAGERY fits because authors use sensory details to make scenes, feelings, and ideas more vivid.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Hints that suggest events still to come
clues.hint: A warning early in a story may prepare readers for a later problem.
clues.definition: Foreshadowing is the use of clues or hints that prepare readers for later events.
clues.signal: Hints and events still to come point to a technique that builds expectation.
clues.explanation: FORESHADOWING fits because writers plant early details that become more meaningful when later events occur.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Scene that interrupts the present action to show an earlier event
clues.hint: It may reveal a memory that explains a character's current choice.
clues.definition: A flashback is a scene or passage that moves back to an earlier time in the story.
clues.signal: Earlier event interrupting present action signals a shift in narrative time.
clues.explanation: FLASHBACK fits because it lets readers learn past information that affects the meaning of the current story.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Perspective from which a story is told
clues.hint: First person and third person are common types.
clues.definition: Point of view is the perspective or position from which a narrative is presented.
clues.signal: Perspective from which a story is told identifies a narration concept.
clues.explanation: POINTOFVIEW fits because it names the narrative perspective that controls what readers know and how events are presented.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Author's choice of words
clues.hint: Formal, casual, precise, or emotional wording can shape meaning.
clues.definition: Diction is an author's word choice and style of expression.
clues.signal: Choice of words directly points to a writer's language decisions.
clues.explanation: DICTION fits because readers analyze selected words to understand tone, meaning, and the author's intended effect.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: How a text is organized
clues.hint: Chronology, comparison, and cause-effect are possible patterns.
clues.definition: Structure is the way parts of a text are organized and connected.
clues.signal: How a text is organized points to the arrangement of its parts.
clues.explanation: STRUCTURE fits because readers examine organization to understand how ideas, scenes, or arguments build on each other.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Central struggle between opposing forces in a story
clues.hint: It may be internal, external, or both.
clues.definition: Conflict is the struggle between opposing forces that drives a story or drama.
clues.signal: Central struggle and opposing forces identify a major story element.
clues.explanation: CONFLICT fits because plot often develops as characters face problems, choices, or opposition.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Method an author uses to reveal a character's traits
clues.hint: Actions, dialogue, thoughts, and descriptions can all do this work.
clues.definition: Characterization is the way an author develops and reveals a character's traits.
clues.signal: Reveal a character's traits points to how readers learn who a character is.
clues.explanation: CHARACTERIZATION fits because it includes both direct description and indirect evidence from what characters say, think, and do.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Sequence of events in a story
clues.hint: It includes what happens and how events connect.
clues.definition: Plot is the organized sequence of events in a story or drama.
clues.signal: Sequence of events identifies a basic narrative element.
clues.explanation: PLOT fits because it names the chain of actions and events that moves a story forward.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Opening background that introduces setting, characters, or situation
clues.hint: This early story part helps readers understand the starting point.
clues.definition: Exposition is background information that introduces key story elements such as setting, characters, and situation.
clues.signal: Opening background and introductions point to an early narrative function.
clues.explanation: EXPOSITION fits because it gives readers the context needed before the main complications fully develop.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Highest-tension turning point in a story
clues.hint: After this moment, the main problem usually moves toward being settled.
clues.definition: The climax is the major turning point or moment of greatest tension in a story.
clues.signal: Highest tension and turning point identify a key plot moment.
clues.explanation: CLIMAX fits because it is the story moment when the central conflict reaches its most intense or decisive point.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Part of a story where main problems are settled
clues.hint: It often follows the moment of highest tension.
clues.definition: Resolution is the part of a story in which central problems are settled or outcomes become clear.
clues.signal: Problems are settled points to the closing function of a plot.
clues.explanation: RESOLUTION fits because readers look there to see how conflicts end and what has changed for the characters.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Restatement of an idea in new words
clues.hint: It keeps the meaning but changes the wording.
clues.definition: A paraphrase is a restatement of a text or idea using different wording while preserving meaning.
clues.signal: Restatement in new words points to a comprehension and writing tool.
clues.explanation: PARAPHRASE fits because it shows understanding by expressing the same idea accurately in different language.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Note added to a text while reading closely
clues.hint: It might mark a question, connection, or important detail in the margin.
clues.definition: An annotation is a note or mark added to a text to record thinking, questions, or observations.
clues.signal: Note added to a text points to an active reading practice.
clues.explanation: ANNOTATION fits because readers use margin notes and marks to track evidence, confusion, patterns, and interpretations.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Category such as poem, play, novel, biography, or myth
clues.hint: It helps set expectations for form, content, and conventions.
clues.definition: Genre is a category of literature or text defined by shared forms, purposes, or conventions.
clues.signal: Category and examples such as poem or novel point to a classification term.
clues.explanation: GENRE fits because readers use it to predict features and compare texts with similar conventions.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Grouped set of lines in a poem
clues.hint: It works somewhat like a paragraph in poetry.
clues.definition: A stanza is a grouped set of lines in a poem, often separated by space from other groups.
clues.signal: Grouped set of lines in a poem identifies a poetry structure term.
clues.explanation: STANZA fits because poems often organize lines into these units to shape rhythm, meaning, and emphasis.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Story written to be performed by actors
clues.hint: Scripts, dialogue, stage directions, and scenes are common features.
clues.definition: Drama is literature written to be performed by actors before an audience.
clues.signal: Performed by actors points to a literary form meant for the stage or screen.
clues.explanation: DRAMA fits because it is read as a script and understood through dialogue, action, scenes, and stage directions.

clues.subject: english-language-arts
clues.clue: Feeling or atmosphere a text creates for readers
clues.hint: Dark imagery and tense pacing can create a fearful one.
clues.definition: Mood is the feeling or atmosphere that a text creates for readers.
clues.signal: Feeling or atmosphere created for readers identifies an effect of language and setting.
clues.explanation: MOOD fits because readers describe the emotional atmosphere produced by details, pacing, setting, and word choice.
